Thinking Machines Lab has unveiled Inkling 2 Mini, a surprisingly capable new open-weight AI model that packs just 26 billion parameters while delivering impressive performance in coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. More importantly, the model can run entirely offline on consumer hardware, including Apple MacBooks equipped with 32GB of unified memory.

Announced on November 20, Inkling 2 Mini arrives as a considerably smaller alternative to the company's massive 594-billion-parameter Inkling 2 Small. However, rather than simply shrinking an existing architecture, Thinking Machines has adopted an interesting approach that allows its new model to perform additional reasoning without generating more tokens. [...] Nevertheless, the company's experiments found that the model's written reasoning remained understandable, without a meaningful reduction in monitorability at this scale. The researchers also acknowledged limitations, including weaker performance on complex multi-turn conversations and instructions involving numerous constraints.

Inkling 2 Mini is now available under the Apache 2.0 license, with downloadable weights on Hugging Face, local deployment through Ollama, and inference and fine-tuning through Thinking Machines' Tinker platform.

For developers interested in running capable AI agents locally rather than relying exclusively on cloud infrastructure, Inkling 2 Mini represents another interesting development in making advanced AI models more accessible. [...] The company claims this approach delivers particularly impressive improvements in agentic coding. Inkling 2 Mini achieved 48.2% on DeepSWE v1.1, compared with 42.2% for Qwen3.8-27B, while its SWE-bench Pro v2 Hard score reached 77.9%, surpassing the latter's 73.8%.

It also scored 46.5% on the Vals Index v2.2 and 79.2% on SWE-bench Verified. These are company-reported evaluation results, and differences in testing configurations mean they shouldn't be interpreted as universal performance advantages.

results.title: Meet Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Mini: 26B Looped MoE Runs on a 32GB Mac - MarkTechPost
results.content:
Thinking Machines Lab has released Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weight looped transformer with 26.4B total parameters. The model reuses its middle layers 3 times per token instead of adding more weights. That keeps the checkpoint near 20GB, small enough for a 32GB Mac or 1 NVIDIA DGX Spark. For developers, Inkling 2 Mini is a local option for agentic coding, tool use and document work. It ships under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face, with hosted inference and fine-tuning on Tinker.

## TL;DR [...] ## TL;DR

- Size: 26.4B total, 3.4B active (5.4B effective per token with looping), up to 1M-token context.
- Runs on: Apple silicon with 32GB+ memory, 1 NVIDIA DGX Spark, or GPUs with 32GB+ VRAM. GGUF builds via Unsloth and llama.cpp.
- Performance: 20.1 on the Artificial Analysis Index, tied with Qwen3.8-27B (self-reported).
- Best: 79.2% on SWE-bench Verified (bash only).
- Worst: 15.2% on HLE-Diamond and 50.0% on MultiChallenge.
- Bottom line: Best: strong agentic coding from a 20GB checkpoint. Worst: weaker knowledge recall and multi-turn instruction following.

## What is Inkling 2 Mini?

Inkling 2 Mini is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model from Thinking Machines that loops its middle layers. It accepts text and images and returns text only. [...] ## Key Takeaways

- Inkling 2 Mini loops 24 stored layers into 48 layer passes per token.
- 26.4B total, 3.4B active, ~20GB, Apache 2.0, up to 1M context.
- Runs on a 32GB Mac or 1 DGX Spark via Ollama, vLLM or llama.cpp.
- Scores 79.2% on SWE-bench Verified and ties Qwen3.8-27B at 20.1 AA Index.
- Weak spots: knowledge recall, multi-turn chat and constraint-heavy prompts.

results.title: Inkling 2 Mini on Mac: Requirements, Ollama, vs Qwen
results.content:
> Some of you thought that Inkling 2 Small was too big at 594B parameters. We heard you: Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer with just 26B parameters, small enough to run on your laptop, powerful enough for agentic work with a score of 20.1 on AA Index.  
> 

## Inkling 2 Mini Requirements: Which Mac Can Run It?

Inkling 2 Mini needs about 20GB of memory in its official form, so the supported setup is an Apple silicon Mac with 32GB or more. That covers a MacBook Air, MacBook Pro, Mac mini or Mac Studio with enough memory. The model card lists “Apple silicon devices with 32GB or more memory (MacBooks, Mac minis and Studios)” next to NVIDIA’s DGX Spark. Compressed community files lower the bar to 16GB. [...] Inkling 2 Mini is the first model from Thinking Machines Lab that fits on a laptop. Released on November 20, 2026, it has 26.4B parameters with 3.4B active, a download of about 20GB, and an Apache 2.0 license. Thinking Machines and Ollama both name the same minimum: an Apple silicon Mac with 32GB of memory or more.

That 32GB line is only half the answer. Unsloth’s compressed versions bring Inkling 2 Mini down to 17.6GB at 4-bit and about 9GB at 1-bit. That puts 16GB and 24GB Macs in range, with some loss in quality. This guide matches every Mac memory size to the right file and walks through the Ollama setup. It also compares Inkling 2 Mini with Qwen 3.8 27B, the local model Thinking Machines measures it against.

## The Key Takeaways [...] ## The Verdict

Inkling 2 Mini is the best-scoring open coding agent under 100B parameters on Thinking Machines’ own tests, and it fits a 32GB Mac. It is also the first proof that Thinking Machines’ looped design works at laptop size. On a 32GB Mac, install Ollama and run it: it is free, private and one command away. On 16GB or 24GB, the compressed files work, but Qwen3.8-27B at a similar compression is the steadier everyday assistant. Pick Inkling 2 Mini for code and search-heavy tasks, Qwen3.8-27B for conversation, and keep both on disk if you have the room.

results.title: Inkling 2 Mini: 26.4B Open-Weight Model, Apache 2.0
results.content:
Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini on November 20, 2026, and it shipped with open weights. The company describes the model as its smallest, a looped transformer that runs on a laptop and excels at agentic coding. TestingCatalog AI News and Quartz both covered the release, and the weights sit on Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 license.

The numbers on the sheet are short but telling. Inkling 2 Mini carries 26.4B total parameters and 3.4B active parameters, it pairs a looped transformer with a mixture-of-experts design, and it lists a 1M-token context window. It accepts text and image inputs and writes text back. Developers can also reach it through Tinker, the company’s platform for inference and customization. [...] The official product description is short enough to quote in full. Thinking Machines calls it “Our smallest model, a looped transformer that runs on a laptop and excels at agentic coding.” Three claims sit in that sentence. The model is small relative to the rest of the lineup, it runs on laptop hardware, and it is good at agentic coding. The first is a matter of record. The second and third are marketing claims until someone measures them.

The phrase smallest model also tells us something by omission. A company only calls one model its smallest when larger ones exist or are planned. The sources cited here name no sibling models, so treat any talk of a full Inkling 2 lineup as unconfirmed until Thinking Machines publishes it.

## Inkling 2 Mini Specs at a Glance [...] The sources confirm the architecture label and nothing more. They do not say how many times the layers loop, whether the loop count changes at inference time, or how looping interacts with the expert routing. Those details decide whether the design delivers on the laptop promise, and they will come out of the technical documentation and early community tests.

## The 1M-Token Context Window

A 1M-token context window puts Inkling 2 Mini in the same headline range as the largest hosted models. Google’s Gemini 4 Neon also lists 1M tokens of context, as our report on Gemini 4 Neon pricing and thinking levels covered. The difference is that Neon runs on Google’s servers, while Inkling 2 Mini ships as weights you can host yourself.
